fields.quote: Moving cache invalidation after a database commit clears one stale-fill race. An older read can still repopulate the cache afterward.

The dek limits itself to one race and a possibility (can). The probes are gated schedules, not a proof of every interleaving.

fields.quote: A cache that remembers database reads
fields.rationale: source.unchanged / functions.mjs read: on miss it awaits db.read and cache.set, so later hits return the saved value.

fields.quote: Moss Catalog shares one synchronous Map between reads and updates. A cache hit returns immediately; a miss asks the database and saves the result. The database captures its read snapshot when called, although the promise can resolve later.
fields.rationale: Matches contracts 1 and 3 and the read function. Later sentences: read is unchanged (contract 4); nothing checks for a write while db.read is pending; cache.set always stores the arrived snapshot. That matches read with no generation check. The embedded {{CODE:0}} is the unchanged reader.
Section label. It does not assert a program fact.

fields.quote: Clearing too early leaves stale data behind
fields.rationale: source.before deletes then awaits db.write. before.fillDuringWrite keeps overlappingRead, cached, and nextRead as old while stored is new.

fields.quote: Before the change, both the overlapping reader and the next reader receive old, even though storage contains new.
fields.rationale: source.before deletes before the write and never deletes again. before.fillDuringWrite: overlappingRead old, nextRead old, stored new. The miss-and-fill-during-wait story is the fillDuringWrite schedule in probe.mjs (writer starts, reader snapshots old, reader fills, then write commits). Explicit promise gates rather than timing guesses matches probe.mjs assumptions. Modal could is right: this is one gated order.
Section label. It does not assert a program fact.

fields.quote: Commit first, then remove the entry
fields.rationale: source.after / functions.mjs after: await db.write then cache.delete. Contract 2: commit happens before fulfillment.

fields.quote: In the supplied results, the overlapping reader still receives old, but the next read fetches new. A rejected write skips deletion, preserving the existing cache entry while storage stays unchanged.
fields.rationale: after() only deletes after a successful await db.write. after.fillDuringWrite: overlappingRead old, cached null, nextRead new. after.failedWrite: cachedAfterUpdate old, stored old, error write. Contract 2: rejection leaves storage unchanged. Late-snapshot paragraph matches overlapping(fn, true) in probe.mjs and both lateSnapshot rows: snapshot old, commit and delete, then cache.set(old); nextRead old under before and after. Commit-before-fulfillment plus delete-after-await is why a fill that finished during the write is gone in fillDuringWrite; that is the modeled order, not every schedule.
Section label. It does not assert a program fact.
fillDuringWrite.nextRead changes from old (before) to new (after). lateSnapshot.nextRead stays old in both. One modeled race versus another, not a universal close.

fields.quote: Post-write deletion clears stale fills that finish before invalidation and avoids eviction on failed writes. It does not support the author's broader claim that concurrent stale reads disappear.
fields.rationale: after.fillDuringWrite leaves cached null and nextRead new. after.failedWrite leaves cachedAfterUpdate old versus before.failedWrite null. source.body: the author says invalidating after the write removes stale cache reads, including concurrent readers. after.fillDuringWrite.overlappingRead is still old, and both lateSnapshot.nextRead values are old, so that claim is not shown. Contract 4: read has no generation check or in-flight synchronization. The disappear wording is a paraphrase of source.body, not a new program claim.
